title: Routing policy header TTL caused sticky fallback to wrong model variant
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During a capacity degradation event on 2026-03-09 we observed a persistent fallback path that routed traffic to a deprecated model variant in a secondary region. The routing decision became "sticky" for affected sessions because a new routing policy field (x-routing-ttl) was misinterpreted by the routing tier. This led to degraded latency and a small percentage of user requests returning outputs from an older, higher-latency variant. This ticket documents the postmortem, telemetry gaps, mitigations applied, and follow-up action items.
impact: ~3.4% of production requests during the 22:10-23:45 UTC window were routed to a deprecated model variant in us-west-2 instead of the intended optimized variant in us-east-1. Average tail latency increased by ~320ms for affected traffic and token cost increased by ~12% for that bucket. No PII or data leakage observed; customer-facing errors minimal but SLA touchpoints triggered for two enterprise customers.
timeline:
2026-03-09 21:58 UTC: Autoscaler started shedding capacity in eu-west-1 due to transient GPU driver OOMs.
2026-03-09 22:10 UTC: Smart routing policy triggered cross-region reroutes to fallback tier.
2026-03-09 22:17 UTC: First pager (oncall) — elevated error rates and rising tail latency in us-west-2.
2026-03-09 22:24 UTC: Engineering identified outgoing requests carrying x-routing-ttl header with value 'sticky' (legacy boolean semantics) instead of numeric TTL.
2026-03-09 22:35 UTC: Temporary mitigation — roll back policy enforcement to policy v1 to stop new sticky annotations.
2026-03-09 22:42 UTC: Deployed hotfix in routing service: accept legacy and numeric x-routing-ttl forms and normalize before decisioning.
2026-03-09 23:06 UTC: Traffic gradually returned to normal variant; latency and cost metrics trended down.
2026-03-09 23:45 UTC: Incident declared resolved for customer impact; follow-up items opened.
root_cause: 1) Protocol mismatch: A newer routing policy introduced an 'x-routing-ttl' header intended to be a numeric TTL (seconds) but was deployed with a client-side component that still emitted the legacy 'sticky' boolean token for long-lived sessions. 2) Parsing asymmetry: The routing tier's parser treated any non-numeric x-routing-ttl as a high-priority sticky flag, causing requests to be pinned to the fallback variant for the full sticky window. 3) Telemetry blind spot: There was insufficient per-request routing-decision tagging in traces to immediately correlate header values with decision outcomes, delaying diagnosis by ~15 minutes.
mitigations:
- Immediate rollback of the policy enforcement that interpreted 'sticky' as an authoritative TTL.
- Hotfix to normalize x-routing-ttl values to numeric TTLs at ingress and log normalization events.
- Manual invalidation of active sticky sessions for affected customer namespaces to force re-evaluation.
- Communication sent to ops and two affected customers with description and timeline.
resolution: Hotfix merged: GH PR #4632 (routing: normalize x-routing-ttl inputs) and rolled to canary within 21 minutes of detection; full rollout by 22:42 UTC. Rollback of policy change to v1 prevented new 'sticky' annotations from being honored. Monitoring alerts refined to detect non-numeric TTLs in routing headers and emit a high-priority signal.
action_items: ENG-16890: Add strict schema validation for routing policy headers at the control plane (owner: Elena García, estimate: 2) - Due 2026-03-18
ENG-16902: Instrument per-request routing decision tags in tracing (owner: Marcus Liu, estimate: 3) - Due 2026-03-21
ENG-16891: Backfill historical routing logs to identify sessions affected in last 90 days and notify customers if needed (owner: Priya Menon, estimate: 4) - Due 2026-03-25
ENG-16910: Update client SDKs and internal annotators to emit numeric TTLs and provide compatibility shim for legacy boolean 'sticky' values (owner: Tomas Novak, estimate: 3) - Due 2026-04-01
ENG-16911: Add alert that triggers when >0.5% of routing headers are non-numeric over 5m window (owner: Observability, estimate: 1) - Due 2026-03-16
ENG-16912: Post-deployment QA checklist to include header schema roundtrip tests and chaos test for policy changes (owner: QA Team, estimate: 2) - Due 2026-03-20
follow_up_notes:
- Short-term hotfix works but is a bandaid; long-term must be schema-first for policy rollout.
- Consider a deprecation timeline for legacy 'sticky' semantics documented in the routing policy RFC.
- Evaluate adding 'routing-decision' sampling to the per-model telemetry pipeline to make root causes for future incidents visible within 5 minutes.
